pairs.subject: agent-browser-control
pairs.evidence: crates/engine-browser/src/lib.rs:1423 Browser actions resolve a caller-written CSS selector to whichever element find_element returns, with no snapshot, runtime reference or match-count refusal, so a flow an agent enqueues through MCP can act on the wrong element of an arbitrary page.

techniques.evidence: crates/engine-browser/src/lib.rs:1423 The caller composes the selector and it is used directly. The engine has no accessibility walk, reference table or clear-on-navigation, and more than one match is not refused. A zero-match miss is at least recorded as SelectorMissing.

crates/engine-browser/src/lib.rs:911 Driver text is interpolated at the call site with no next step, and the same shape recurs for new_page, the listeners and content, so there is no single rewriting door. The MCP fetch tool passes errors to the agent via e.to_string(). budget_exhausted (line 226) and StepOutcome are good partial realizations.

crates/engine-browser/src/lib.rs:1137 Reversibility is a caller's position in the request, not a per-command class. TransactRequest::validate checks only the idempotency key and profile, so a Click placed in steps is re-issued by both commit passes with nothing consuming a class. The structural hold-back of submit_action is sound but is not a command registry.

crates/engine-browser/src/lib.rs:8 Chrome is held in-process by the long-lived server, so there is no separate daemon to discover through a state file or probe for busy versus dead. The warm-session goal is met by holders and a persistent user-data-dir, and a crash is recovered on the next acquire.

crates/engine-browser/src/lib.rs:615 The engine drives Chrome through an in-process CDP handle. A search of this file for TcpListener, .bind( and remote-debugging found no listener, and nothing forwards a browser command surface. engine-remote proxies HTTP fetches to peer nodes, not browser control.

pairs.registryProposal: The subject assumes an interactive snapshot-act loop and does not say how references-over-selectors applies to a pre-declared batch flow, where the action list is authored before any page is read and no snapshot step can precede it. A ruling on that shape (for example a separate discovery run that returns references, or an explicit exemption) would make the verdict less dependent on interpretation.
